compiled_state.title: Test creation calibration (c): feedback loop from production bugs and review findings to test-creation prompts
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

When bugs surface in production OR are caught by code review rather than by the test suite, the project today has no mechanism for the test-writing agents to learn from that miss. The same class of bug recurs. Test-writing sub-agents (red-test-writer, sprint task-execution, fix-bug RED-phase) operate against static guidance (behavioral-testing-standard.md) that doesn't grow from observed misses. This epic delivers a closed-loop feedback system: closed bugs with extractable lessons get `NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE:` JSON comments + `negative-example` tag during /dso:fix-bug Phase G; test-writing sub-agents consume retrieved examples via `negative-examples-lookup.sh` at task start; recurring patterns graduate to universal rules in `behavioral-testing-standard.md` via /dso:retro Graduation Phase with human approval. After this epic ships, test-writing agents see project-specific "Lessons from past bugs" alongside the universal 7-rule standard — where today they see only the standard.

Users affected: DSO maintainer, sprint orchestrators, test-writing sub-agents (red-test-writer, sprint task-execution, fix-bug RED-phase), code-reviewer-test-quality, completion-verifier, and downstream calibration consumers (411b-a047 mutation infrastructure, 7f42-e41f growth metrics, fb3e-b01b deeper signals).

## Success Criteria

SC1: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/negative-example-comment.md published. NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment schema: {schema_version=1, bug_type_slug (string; from 4911-c7ba taxonomy), intent_ids_if_applicable (array of intent_ids from 94ed manifest entries; values MUST reference real manifest entries OR be empty), missed_signal_summary (describes what FAILED to be detected — canonical example in contract showing correct polarity), what_test_would_have_caught_it, generalizable_lesson, related_files (array of paths), scope_claim ("this pattern applies to any agent that..."), falsification ("this would NOT apply when...")}. Contract document includes prompt-engineering guidance for sonnet extraction to avoid inverted-polarity drafts AND a consistent style guide for opus drafting graduation rules (matching the existing 7-rule standard's structure).

SC2: /dso:fix-bug Phase G extended. EXECUTES AFTER 4911-c7ba bug-type classification step (explicit ordering — Phase G runs after 4911 sets bug_type_<slug> tag). When a bug ticket is closed with reason="Fixed: ...":
(i) sonnet sub-agent evaluates extraction conditions: bug not caught by an existing test AND pattern generalizable;
(ii) MANDATORY pre-extraction redaction step: sonnet identifies and redacts credentials, tokens, keys, PII, customer/user identifiers, internal-only IDs from all string fields. If sonnet cannot confidently redact, MUST skip extraction;
(iii) output MUST include scope_claim AND falsification fields per SC1; if either is vacuous ("when the code is correct", "always applies"), skip extraction;
(iv) atomic write: NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment + negative-example tag applied as single unit (rollback if either fails);
(v) when 4911 classification failed (bug_type_<slug> not set on the ticket), use bug_type_slug="unclassified" and add `retro-needs-classification` tag;
(vi) SKIP_RECORD comment logged on every skip with {decision: "skip", skip_reason: <one sentence>} for audit trail;
(vii) intent_ids_if_applicable values validated at write time against 94ed manifest entries; invalid intent_ids cause write to fail OR values dropped with warning.

SC3: plugins/dso/scripts/negative-examples-lookup.sh <task-id-or-args> implements retrieval:
(a) reads task's file_impact + claimable_intent from ticket data;
(b) queries via existing ticket-CLI primitives: `ticket list --type=bug --status=closed --has-tag=negative-example --has-tag=bug-type-<slug>`;
(c) excludes tickets with any `promoted-to-standard:*` tag;
(d) excludes stale examples: tickets whose related_files reference paths not present on disk (auto-staleness check);
(e) relevance ranking: narrower-scoped bugs (smaller related_files set) preferred, weight by recency. When two examples have identical relevance scores, deterministic tie-breaking via ticket-id lexical order;
(f) returns top-N=3 most relevant matches as JSON;
(g) output includes excluded_count field (signal for /dso:retro Graduation Phase when count is high);
(h) summary format per match: {slug, missed_signal_summary, generalizable_lesson} (concise, not full schema);
(i) ARG_MAX-safe via --output-file flag.

SC4: Three test-writing sub-agent prompts updated to invoke `negative-examples-lookup.sh` at task-start: plugins/dso/agents/red-test-writer.md, plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/task-execution.md, and the fix-bug RED-phase prompt (concrete path under plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/ resolved during implementation-plan). Retrieved examples are injected with explicit label "## Project-specific learned patterns (advisory; not universal Rule 1-7+ authority)" so the agent distinguishes project-specific learned guidance from universal Rule 1-7 standards. Cap at 3 examples per task. When 0 examples returned (e.g., cold-start), section omitted entirely (no empty block, no error).

SC5: /dso:retro extended with a Graduation Phase. Opus sub-agent reads all bugs with `negative-example` tag AND without `promoted-to-standard:*` tag via single CLI query. Identifies graduation candidates via two trigger paths:
(a) Frequency floor: ≥3 examples sharing the same bug_type_slug AND distinct root-cause fingerprints. Opus MUST verify <80% missed_signal_summary similarity across the group; groups whose examples are >=80% similar are collapsed as a single signal (treats as 1 example, not N).
(b) Cross-slug semantic match: opus identifies a pattern via SINGLE FALSIFIABLE PREDICATE naming a specific testable condition (e.g., "all four miss the case where X is empty"). Theme-level labels (e.g., "all four are about validation") are NOT permitted — predicate must name a specific input state or code path AND an expected observable outcome.
Each candidate is surfaced with:
(1) 4-field draft rule matching the existing behavioral-testing-standard.md structure: {rule_statement, rationale, anti_pattern_example, correct_pattern_example};
(2) evidence_citations: ≥3 bug IDs with quoted missed_signal_summary from each;
(3) explicit provenance ("3 same-slug bugs" OR "opus cross-slug semantic match across N examples").
PRE-DRAFT VALIDATION: opus MUST check existing rules in behavioral-testing-standard.md; if proposed rule overlaps an existing rule, opus either revises to propose modification to existing rule OR justifies distinct coverage. Block surfacing if conflict is unresolved.
SYCOPHANCY GATE: on user acceptance, before PR is drafted, user must answer challenge: "Where does this rule add distinct coverage beyond existing Rules 1-N?" An empty answer OR an answer that restates the rule blocks the PR and marks the candidate as `challenged-rejected`.

SC6: Atomic graduation: on accepted candidate, PR is drafted FIRST (contains the standard amendment); contributing bug tickets get `promoted-to-standard:<rule-id>` tag ONLY after PR creation succeeds. If PR draft fails, no tags are applied — prevents phantom graduation records.

SC7: behavioral-testing-standard.md remains designated a safeguard file per a03c-d55e's SC2 / CLAUDE.md rule 22. /dso:retro Graduation Phase MUST surface candidates and draft rule text but MUST NOT auto-commit. Human approval to merge the PR remains required.

SC8: Lifecycle hook — status transition closed→open on a tagged bug automatically removes the negative-example tag (sentry on the ticket-transition hook). Verified by SC9(i) fixture: reopening a tagged bug removes the tag and the bug is excluded from subsequent lookup results.

SC9: Synthetic end-to-end test covering twelve scenarios:
(a) EXTRACTION + atomic write + audit trail: fixture bug with test-miss + generalizable pattern produces NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment + negative-example tag atomically.
(b) SKIP recorded: fixture bug where extraction conditions not met → SKIP_RECORD comment with decision and reason.
(c) PRIVACY redaction: fixture bug with token/credential in description → redaction confirmed in NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comment OR extraction skipped.
(d) LOOKUP with stale-example exclusion: fixture bug whose related_files references a deleted path → excluded from lookup output.
(e) FREQUENCY graduation: 3 fixture bugs sharing bug_type_slug=X with distinct root-cause fingerprints → /dso:retro Graduation surfaces candidate with provenance "3 same-slug bugs"; user accepts; PR draft + promoted-to-standard:<rule-id> tagging.
(f) FREQUENCY COLLAPSE: 3 fixture bugs sharing bug_type_slug with >=80% missed_signal_summary similarity → collapsed as 1 signal, no candidate surfaced.
(g) CROSS-SLUG predicate graduation: 4 fixture bugs across 2 slugs sharing a falsifiable predicate ("all four miss the case where input array is empty") → candidate surfaced with provenance "opus cross-slug semantic match across 4 examples".
(h) THEME-only rejection: 4 fixture bugs share a theme ("all about validation") without a specific predicate → NOT surfaced.
(i) SYCOPHANCY challenge blocks empty response: user accepts candidate, then enters empty answer to "where does this rule add distinct coverage?" → PR is blocked, candidate marked challenged-rejected.
(j) COLD_START / EMPTY_CORPUS: fixture task in a project with zero closed bugs tagged negative-example → lookup returns empty result with excluded_count=0; test-writer prompt omits "Lessons from past bugs" section entirely (no error, no hang).
(k) RANKING_TIE: 2 fixture examples with identical relevance scores → lookup returns them in deterministic ticket-id lexical order.
(l) OPERATIONAL METRIC EMISSION: /dso:retro Graduation Phase emits structured telemetry to a RETRO_TELEMETRY: ticket comment OR a retro-telemetry-<timestamp>.json artifact with fields {examples_extracted_since_last_retro, examples_skipped_count, graduation_candidates_surfaced, candidates_accepted, sycophancy_rejections, candidates_rejected_predicate, candidates_rejected_frequency_collapse}.

## Approach

Four sequential phases, each independently mergeable:
- Phase 1: SC1 (contract) + SC2 (recording with redaction, atomicity, audit trail, intent_ids validation).
- Phase 2: SC3 (lookup helper with relevance + staleness + tie-breaking) + SC4 (test-writer prompt integration).
- Phase 3: SC5 + SC6 + SC7 (graduation with predicate/distinct-root validation + sycophancy gate + atomic PR-first + safeguard preservation).
- Phase 4: SC8 + SC9 (lifecycle hooks + twelve-scenario end-to-end synthetic test).

## Scenario Analysis (Blue Team surviving)

- Sonnet over-extraction (high/extraction-quality): partially mitigated by SC2(i) generalizability check + SC2(iii) scope_claim/falsification requirement + SC2(vi) audit trail; residual is sonnet's self-assessment quality.
- Sonnet under-extraction (high/extraction-quality): partially mitigated by SC2(vi) SKIP_RECORD audit trail; residual is silent signal loss; /dso:retro can surface high-skip-rate trends.
- Cross-slug opus over-clustering (high/promotion-integrity): partially mitigated by SC5(b) single-falsifiable-predicate constraint + SYCOPHANCY gate + PRE-DRAFT conflict check; residual is opus's self-assessment of predicate quality.
- Standard amendment too narrow (medium/rule-quality): partially mitigated by SC2(iii) scope_claim/falsification + SYCOPHANCY gate; no minimum-breadth requirement.
- Standard amendment too broad (medium/rule-quality): partially mitigated by SC5 PRE-DRAFT conflict check; overlap is opus's semantic judgment.
- File-impact intersection false positive (high/retrieval-relevance): partially mitigated by SC3(e) narrower-scoped + recency ranking; no semantic relevance filter.
- Top-N cutoff silences critical examples (high/retrieval-coverage): partially mitigated by SC3(f) excluded_count signal in output; ranking heuristic is structural not semantic.
- Cross-epic standard amendment conflicts (high/rule-quality): partially mitigated by SC5 PRE-DRAFT check against committed state of standard; concurrent in-flight PRs not visible.
- intent_id schema mismatch (medium/schema-integrity): mitigated by SC2(vii) validation against 94ed manifest entries.
- Bug ticket comment bloat (medium/data-integrity): partially mitigated by SC8 reopening-removes-tag + SC2(iv) atomic write; deduplication of multiple NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE comments on same ticket not specified (acceptable — latest comment wins in retrieval implicitly).

## Out of Scope

- Strict ownership enforcement at the manifest layer (explicitly out per 94ed brainstorm).
- Concurrent /dso:retro telemetry write conflict (deferred — low probability; manageable via lock or merge-by-comment-id).
- Operational metric dashboards beyond raw telemetry emission (deferred to /dso:retro-stats or similar observability epic).
- Cross-PR amendment conflict detection (deferred — relies on committed state of standard; PR-review process catches conflicts).

## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation Override, 2026-05-18)

### External-dependency verification — addressable touchpoints (Probe-6 partial remediation with explicit override)

The 2026-05-16 audit flagged probe 6 over three external touchpoints. Two are in-session-verifiable via the available CLIs; one is genuinely external and explicitly overridden as non-gating with a documented residual.

| Touchpoint | In-session verification | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| SC5 sycophancy gate user response | If the gate fires during the 69e8 sprint, the user's response is captured in the same session transcript. Verification: `grep -E 'sycophancy.*(rejected\|accepted\|deferred)' <session-transcript-or-PIL>` returns ≥1 entry OR the absence is documented as "gate did not fire in this sprint window" — sprint cannot close without one of these states recorded. | IN-SESSION ✓ |
| SC6 atomic graduation depends on gh PR creation | `command -v gh && gh auth status \|\| gh auth login` runs at sprint Phase A; an atomic-graduation invocation during the sprint exercises the gh-PR-creation path against a synthetic fixture branch and asserts a successful PR creation + immediate close. Verification: `gh pr create --draft --base <fixture-base> --head <fixture-head> --title "atomic-graduation-dogfooding" --body "..."` returns a URL; `gh pr close <pr>` succeeds. | IN-SESSION ✓ |
| SC7 human-approval merge on the safeguard-file PR | Human reviewer approval and merge on the `behavioral-testing-standard.md` amendment PR is **genuinely external** — no in-session command can synthesize human review. | OPERATIONAL RESIDUAL (override) |

### Explicit override note

SC7's human-approval requirement is acknowledged as operationally external. Sprint closure does NOT gate on the PR being merged within the sprint; closure DOES require that:
- The amendment PR has been **opened** (`gh pr view <pr-number> --json state` returns `"OPEN"` or `"MERGED"`),
- The PR is **assigned to a human reviewer** (`gh pr view <pr-number> --json reviewRequests --jq 'length'` returns ≥1),
- The deferral of merge-approval is recorded as a sprint Phase I comment noting the outstanding human-action item.

This converts the audit's prose-only external dependency into structured in-session preflight + an explicit operational-residual carve-out. The audit's "structured External Dependencies block" pattern is honored in substance (ownership/handling/access/verification_command columns are implicit in the table) while respecting that human review is non-gating.
## Dependencies

- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration) — required. SC7 enforces a03c's safeguard-file designation for behavioral-testing-standard.md; SC5's PRE-DRAFT validation reads the standard structure a03c established.
- 4911-c7ba (Bug-classification coverage registry) — required. SC2 executes after 4911's bug-type-<slug> classification; SC3 retrieval queries by 4911's slug taxonomy; SC5(a) frequency trigger groups by slug.
- 94ed-f55c (Plan-time intent allocation manifest) — required. SC1 intent_ids_if_applicable references 94ed manifest entries; SC2(vii) validates intent_ids at write time; SC3 reads task claimable_intent from manifest entries.
- d566-afa6 (Generation-time prevention) — required. SC4's test-writer prompts are the same files d566 modifies with Rule 6/7. Coordination: when both epics ship in overlapping sprints, merge-window protocol applies to those prompt files.

## Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2): not triggered. Sufficient context inherited from prior calibration brainstorms.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 20 red-team scenarios surfaced; 10 mitigated-by-spec after blue-team filter; 10 surviving (most LLM-judgment residual, partial-mitigated).
- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): 2 conflicts (a03c safeguard, d566 same-prompts overlap — both managed), 2 considerations (4911 taxonomy, 94ed intent vocabulary), 3 benign (411b, 7f42, cf7b).
- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal — modifies /dso:fix-bug Phase G, test-writer prompts, /dso:retro). Five risks folded: SCOPE_CLAIM + FALSIFICATION fields in extraction (SC2(iii)), SKIP_RECORD audit trail (SC2(vi)), structured graduation drafting with evidence_citations (SC5), single-falsifiable-predicate constraint for cross-slug (SC5(b)), sycophancy challenge gate (SC5).
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity (4, 4), Scope (4, 4, 4, 4), Value (4, 4). All dimensions >= 4 after one revision cycle.
- Scale context (Step 0): small-to-medium — dozens of bugs and review findings per quarter; LLM-based extraction is feasible per-event.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 9 (>= 7 threshold) — would route to /dso:preplanning full mode if invoked; preplanning explicitly deferred this session.
- User-directed design decisions during brainstorm: tickets-as-storage (no separate file) with `NEGATIVE_EXAMPLE:` JSON comments; `negative-example` tag set on extraction; `promoted-to-standard:<rule-id>` tag on graduation; recording in /dso:fix-bug (sonnet); promotion in /dso:retro (opus + human approval at safeguard boundary); hybrid promotion triggers (frequency floor ≥3 same-slug + opus cross-slug falsifiable predicate); top-3 retrieval cap with relevance + staleness exclusion; sycophancy challenge gate mirroring 94ed's challenge round pattern.

comments.body: CROSS-EPIC NOTE from 411b-a047-18de-4516: 411b's threshold-breach auto-bug-creation (SC5) is one of 69e8's input signals. Auto-created bugs include a 4-field structured blurb (WHAT/THRESHOLD/CONTEXT/NEXT_STEP) with context about why mutation testing is used in the project. 69e8's negative-example extraction during /dso:fix-bug Phase G will process these bugs the same as human-filed bugs — no special handling required. The bugs include content-hash dedup tags (mutation-breach-<sha>) scoped per-stack-per-source-file, so recurring root-causes naturally dedup across PRs.

comments.body: CROSS-EPIC COORDINATION from cf65-e3b4-0bea-4756: 4911-c7ba child story cf65-e3b4-0bea-4756 adds a detected_by classification field to bug tickets. 69e8's Graduation Phase should consume detected_by tags as a graduation-candidate weighting signal — production-caught (detected_by:production) and review-caught bugs are higher-value graduation candidates than test-caught bugs (which already demonstrate working tests). The field allows /dso:retro to filter graduation candidates by channel via ticket list --has-tag=detected_by:<channel>.

comments.body: UPDATE TO PRIOR COMMENT: the detected_by classification field referenced in the earlier coordination comment (originally story cf65-e3b4-0bea-4756) has been rolled into the new Calibration Program Observability epic a34c-b345-1e63-4ae3. 69e8's graduation phase will be able to use detected_by tags as a candidate-weighting signal once the observability epic ships.
